cycles.cycle: CampaignPricingEngine (Domain) -> App\Services\LoyaltyService / SettingsService / PricingRuleEngine / Pricing\* -> Eloquent models -> Booking model -> LoyaltyService
cycles.root_cause: The pricing calculators are stateless and take Eloquent models as parameters, so the calculation logic is bound to persistence shapes. Relocating them to app/Domain would move the leak rather than remove it, because they would then import App\Models.
cycles.current_behavior: Loyalty point conversion and DB-backed settings reads participate in the campaign price calculation.
cycles.risk: medium - Rule 9 requires pricing determinism, and a DB-backed setting is an external input to the calculation. A settings change alters historical replayability of a price.
cycles.chosen_solution: Leave in place for now and record as architecture debt. The correct end state is value-object parameters on the calculators plus a PricingSettingsProvider contract, which is a financial-determinism change requiring its own approved phase.

cycles.cycle: Booking model events -> app(LoyaltyService, SettingsService, ReferralTrackingService) -> Eloquent models -> Booking model
cycles.root_cause: Domain side effects (loyalty reversal, referral cancellation/refund) were attached as Eloquent model events and therefore have no injectable dependency, forcing service location.
cycles.current_behavior: Every booking status change to cancelled/rejected/refunded/completed automatically reverses points and cancels or refunds referral tracking, inside whatever transaction the caller opened.
cycles.risk: high - these are financial side effects whose transaction timing is implicit and untested in isolation; they also fire for status changes made by reporting-adjacent code paths.
cycles.chosen_solution: Not remediated in Phase 0.13. The behaviour is correct and covered; extracting it would change when the side effects commit, which is a financial-semantics change. Recommended as the first Phase 0.15 item with dedicated coverage.

cycles.cycle: CampaignPricingService -> (previously) 7 unused service deps mirroring CampaignPricingEngine
cycles.root_cause: The legacy wrapper copied the canonical engine's constructor signature when Phase 0.6 extracted the engine, then never used seven of the eight properties.
cycles.current_behavior: Resolved. The wrapper now declares only PricingEngineInterface.
cycles.risk: low - cosmetic dependency-surface inflation that obscured the real Domain->Services coupling.
cycles.chosen_solution: Dead constructor dependencies removed; class retained as a thin compatibility wrapper.

cycles.cycle: CampaignPricingService <-> LoyaltyService (soft cycle named in the Phase 0.2 audit)
cycles.root_cause: CampaignPricingEngine needs loyalty point-value conversion, and LoyaltyService needs booking context. Neither depends on the other in its constructor, so there is no container resolution cycle - but both read the same reward configuration.
cycles.current_behavior: The engine calls LoyaltyService::calculatePointsForAmount(); LoyaltyService never calls back into pricing.
cycles.risk: low-medium - no runtime cycle; the coupling is one-directional today and would become a true cycle if pricing were ever called from inside a loyalty operation.
cycles.chosen_solution: Left as-is and documented. The relationship is one-directional, so no container cycle exists to remove.
